physical_harm: Incise wound caused by a sharp-edged weapon
premeditation_planning: Court found premeditation/planning based on motive
motive: Borrowing money from the deceased and pressure to repay
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court did not accept the circumstantial evidence as sufficient to establish the guilt of the accused, noting contradictions, improbabilities, and inconsistencies in the evidence adduced.
witness_credibility: The court found the witnesses (PW-10, PW-11, and PW-12) to be unreliable, with their statements being improbable, contradictory, and full of coincidences.

legal_representation.accused: Pranab Kumar Mullick, Mrs. Soma Mullick, Anil Rana, Ms. Banani Sikdar, Sebat Kumar Deuria, Sagar Kundu, Rohit Rana, Ajay Solanki, Advs.
legal_representation.state: Ajay Bansal, A.A.G., Gaurav Yadava, Samar Vijay Singh, Keshav Mittal, Ms. Sabarni Som, Ms. Veena Bansal, Saurav Jindal, Sanjay Yadav, Nikilesh Ramachandran, Advs.

appeal_history.trial_court: Convicted under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the IPC
appeal_history.supreme_court: Set aside the judgment and acquitted the appellant

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused were seen with the deceased, there was an extra-judicial confession, and scientific evidence such as blood group matching and recovery of items supported the case of murder.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution's case was based on improbable and contradictory witness statements, and that the evidence did not establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that in cases based on circumstantial evidence, the facts must be consistent with the hypothesis of the guilt of the accused and must exclude every possible hypothesis except that of the accused's guilt.
precedent_relied_upon: Pritinder Singh @ Lovely v. The State of Punjab [2023] 10 S.C.R. 1033: (2023) 7 SCC 727; Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra [1985] 1 SCR 88:(1984) 4 SCC 116
